did_you_know.text: Did you know? The verse describes three stages of distancing oneself from evil: not following the advice of the wicked, not standing in the way of sinners, and not sitting among mockers.
Did you know? The three groups mentioned in the verse—the wicked, sinners, and mockers—represent different negative influences that the blessed person avoids.
Did you know? The opposite of following the way of evil is not merely avoiding it, but also taking delight in the LORD’s instruction and meditating on it day and night.
Did you know? The righteous person is compared to a tree planted beside streams of water: it has a constant source of nourishment, bears fruit in its season, and its leaves do not wither.
Did you know? The verse emphasizes that the fruit is produced “in its season”—that is, growth and ripening take place at the proper time.
Did you know? The wicked are presented as the complete opposite of the firmly planted tree: they are like chaff, a light material that the wind blows away and scatters.
Did you know? The verse distinguishes between two situations: the wicked will not stand in the judgment, and sinners will not be included among the assembly of the righteous.
Did you know? The psalm ends by contrasting two ways: the LORD watches over the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
